text:
maria_finance: Quick FYI  TensorFleet sent their commercial appendix for embeddings + reserved GPU. There are a few billing semantics that look risky for finance. Can procurement/ops/ML glance before I escalate to legal?

leo_procure: Paste the bits that look off.

maria_finance: Snippet from their appendix:

```
Reserved GPU Tier 1: 500 vGPU-hrs/mo @ $5.25/hr
Reserved GPU Tier 2: 1500 vGPU-hrs/mo @ $4.80/hr
Burst: +25% buffer; overage billed at 2x base rate beyond buffer
Embedding SKU: $0.00095 per vector-hour OR $0.00002 per vector-request (mode selectable)
Onboarding: $12k one-time non-refundable
Price experiment clause: vendor may adjust rates +/-12% with 30d notice to "align platform economics"
Invoice: monthly in USD to EU entity
```

anya_ops: Price experiment clause is scary. Also the embedding units again are ambiguous. We need a definition of vector-hour and whether cache/KV hits count.

owen_ml: If they count emitted vectors even for cache hits, any dedupable rerank pipeline will blow the budget. We should ask for a clear dedupe/caching exemption. Also need the algorithm they use to hash vectors and its tolerance.

kate_legal: From a contract perspective: remove unilateral price-change rights or at minimum add a cap (<=5%) for first 12 months and give us termination right for material increases (>5%). Also require written notice + mutual consent for experimental price changes that affect committed customers.

vendor_rep_tensorfleet: Hi team  quick clarifications: vector-hour is defined as "unique emitted vectors served by the model averaged over an hour". Cache hits served from customer-managed KV are not billed. We do run small experimental pricing pilots internally but we can exclude signed commit customers from automatic experiments.

maria_finance: Good start but need examples. Finance asks: 1) sample invoice that maps our telemetry fields to their billed lines, 2) monthly CSV export with per-SKU breakdown, 3) Net-30 payment terms (they propose Net-45), 4) option to invoice to our US entity or fixed FX protection for 12 months.

leo_procure: Procurement asks: convert onboarding fee to usage credit if commit reached within 90 days, pilot PO cap option ($30k) with console cap to block overages, and explicit overage cap during pilot (max $10k).

anya_ops: Ops ask: provide usage API schema (proto/json), and webhook alerts when usage hits >95% of commit. Need a console toggle to disable overages beyond PO cap. Also confirm burst overage calculation is based on daily rolling window, not per-second spikes.

owen_ml: Technical ask: provide the hashing spec for "unique emitted vectors" including quantization/dedup rules and a sample cost calc for a 50k-batch job with 15% cache hit. Also confirm whether batched requests are charged per-request or by exact vector count.

vendor_rep_tensorfleet: We can provide sample invoices, the usage API spec, and the hashing note. We bill exact emitted vectors in per-request mode; per-vector-hour mode measures unique vectors in memory per hour. For enterprise customers we can provide audit logs and agree to a 12-month price-lock on committed SKUs.

kate_legal: Great. Also require SLA credits to be applied as invoice line-item automatically and refundable if not used. Dispute window should be 60 days (their terms say 15). Audit rights: quarterly reconciliation with adjustment for discrepancies >2%.

maria_finance: Add requirement: invoice must include line-itemized GL code mapping and team tag fields so AP can auto-map charges. Without that we need manual recon.

leo_procure: If vendor won't accept pilot protections we propose a capped pilot PO for $30k with explicit overage opt-out and console switch; vendor rep please confirm if this is acceptable to accelerate signing.

vendor_rep_tensorfleet: Cap and pilot opt-out acceptable. We can convert onboarding fee to usage credits if commit reached within 90 days. We'll produce a template invoice and CSV export sample by EOD tomorrow.

anya_ops: One more operational ask: require daily usage delta export so we can reconcile quickly; also require a sample reconciliation run from vendor side showing how their billed units map to our telemetry IDs.

owen_ml: Also ask for a test account where we can run a billing simulation for a week with synthetic traffic to see how different modes bill. That will make cost forecasting accurate.

kate_legal: I'll draft contract language for price-lock, FX handling, SLA credit mechanics, dispute window, and audit rights. Leo, loop me in on the redline.

procurement_bot: Reminder: attach vendor quote, sample invoice template, API spec, and onboarding SOW to Confluence under vendor-evals/TensorFleet. Set decision milestone 2024-11-15.

leo_procure: Thanks all  I'll consolidate asks and send to TensorFleet by EOD. Ping me for urgent changes. :thumbsup:
